specification.problem: Exactly identify an unknown multilinear polynomial f over F_2 in n=3 variables, degree at most 2 (7 coefficients c_0, c_1, c_2, c_3, c_12, c_13, c_23), using a naive derivative-based Bernstein-Vazirani scheme. Coefficients are hard-coded into compiled gates for functional simulation only. No query-complexity claim is made.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Only the tiny instance n=3, d=2, q=2 with a naive 10-qubit identification circuit that recovers all 7 coefficients. It is NOT the paper's O(n^(d-1)) exact quantum algorithm and does not demonstrate any query advantage. Because the coefficients are compiled into the gates, it shows only that the coefficients can be read back from classical build parameters. Out of scope: general q and d, the optimal query construction and orthogonality argument, the lower bound, and any black-box query-count certification.

symbols.meaning: coefficient of the monomial prod_{i in S} x_i
linear part of D_i f restricted to variables j!=i, with l^{(i)}_j=c_{ij}

equations.label: Multilinear polynomial
equations.description: Parametrization of the unknown polynomial with 7 coefficients.
equations.abstract_quote: identify an unknown multilinear polynomial of degree d in n variables over a finite field Fq
equations.justification: The abstract names multilinear polynomials of degree d. The explicit sum form is standard, specialized to q=2, n=3, d=2.

equations.label: Derivative of a multilinear polynomial
equations.description: For degree<=2 multilinear f, the derivative in direction e_i is affine and independent of x_i.
equations.justification: Direct expansion over F_2 using x_i^2=x_i. Used as a candidate degree-reduction step, not claimed to be the paper's method.

equations.label: Restricted phase gate for derivative block
equations.description: Diagonal phase on the 2-qubit register of block i, compiled directly from the classical coefficients: Z on qubit j if c_ij=1, plus a global phase (-1)^{c_i} handled by the ancilla.
equations.justification: Equals f(x'+e_i)+f(x') by eq_2. Compiled with classical coefficients, so no oracle calls are made.

equations.label: Controlled BV block
equations.description: Ancilla a_i in |+> controls the phase (-1)^{b(c_i+l.x')}. H on x' yields |l^{(i)}> and H on a_i yields |c_i>.
equations.justification: Exact BV identity for affine phases with kickback on the ancilla.

equations.label: Constant term
equations.description: The constant f(0)=c_0 is read from a single ancilla by a Z gate if c_0=1. This is a classical shortcut since c_0 is compiled in.

registers.name: x1
registers.role: Qubits 4,5 holding variables (x_2,x_3) for block 1. Output (c_12,c_13).

steps.description: For each i, apply the controlled restricted phase C-U_i with control a_i and target x_i register: CZ(a_i, x_i[j]) if c_ij=1, and Z on a_i if c_i=1.
Apply Z on a0 if c_0=1.
Apply H to all 10 qubits. The final state is a computational basis state encoding all coefficients.

specification.measurement: Circuit is measurement-free. Read the computational basis state of the final state. Qubit 0 gives c_0, qubits 1-3 give c_1..c_3, qubits 4-9 give pairwise coefficients.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Fixed map with qubit indices 0..9, qubit 0 least significant: c_0=q0, c_1=q1, c_2=q2, c_3=q3, c_12=q4 (redundantly q6), c_13=q5 (redundantly q8), c_23=q7 (redundantly q9). Redundant copies must agree.
assumptions: Tiny instance n=3, d=2, q=2 chosen by me
Only monomials with |S|<=2 are accepted, keys outside this set must be rejected, and missing keys mean 0
missing_information: The paper's actual exact O(n^(d-1)) query algorithm and its state-orthogonality construction
